the relationship between oxidative stress and symptom clusters and cognitive function in children with ALL.
the longitudinal relationships of biomarkers of oxidative status, symptom clusters, and cognitive function in children over the 1st year of ALL treatment.

the longitudinal relationships between oxidative stress, symptoms, and cognition were complex and dynamic, and that oxidative stress was associated with symptom distress, but not with cognition.
the GSH biomarker of oxidative stress was associated with the CCSC L, and cognitive function in children with ALL.

the longitudinal parallel process model results indicate that higher levels of oxidative stress at the initial measurement are associated with lower symptom cluster severity, better cognitive function, and better cognitive improvement during treatment for childhood ALL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children with higher levels of oxidative stress at diagnosis have more symptoms and cognitive impairments and those with lower levels have less symptoms and cognitive impairment.
children who have high levels of oxidative biomarkers in their cerebrospinal fluids at the initial measurement have a lower symptom burden and better cognitive function.
children with ALL who have higher GSH biomarkers (lower oxidative stress) at diagnosis have better cognitive functioning and less symptom distress over the first year treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GSH biomarker of oxidative stress can be used to predict the severity of the CCSC L, and the cognitive function and improvement in cognition of children over the first 12 months of ALL treatment.
